final_candidates.decision_summary: Strongest AlphaMissense LOF-proxy signal in the pool with moderate MSA support for functional importance; alanine removes an acidic side chain likely relevant to catalysis/stability.
Consistent with the well-established thermolabile pathogenic MTHFR mechanism and has solid pathogenicity evidence; plausibility/MSA signals are neutral but do not contradict LOF.

Mechanistic candidate: charge-removing substitution at a conserved basic residue in the N-terminal catalytic/FAD-binding region, a classic severe-deficiency pattern; retained despite lacking direct phenotype confirmation.

stop_reason.detail: Tool-call budget for this run has been consumed, so the final ranking is fixed from existing evidence plus mechanistic priors.

history.rationale: Classic human C677T variant (A222V) causing a thermolabile enzyme with strongly reduced folate-dependent activity; well-validated partial LOF that preserves folding enough to be viable.
A222V (C677T) is the classic thermolabile MTHFR variant causing strongly reduced enzyme activity in humans; direct literature knowledge supports LOF direction. Retained pending quantitative evidence.

AlphaMissense 0.632 (pathogenic class) plus zero mutant frequency at a highly conserved position (entropy 2.14, full coverage) supports functional impairment; A222V is also the known thermolability polymorphism site, consistent with reduced activity.
Well-characterized thermolabile pathogenic variant with solid pathogenicity score (z=0.632) and full MSA applicability; known LOF mechanism in humans.
Aspartate in the catalytic domain; loss of the acidic side chain may disrupt active-site electrostatics needed for folate reduction.
Conserved acidic residue in the catalytic/FAD-domain region; alanine substitution plausibly disrupts catalysis. Confidence moderate until MSA/phenotype evidence is gathered.

AlphaMissense LOF proxy is the closest tool to the reward and scores D291A 0.852 (pathogenic), the highest in the pool; D291 is a conserved catalytic-region Asp (NADP/FAD binding lobe), so LOF is mechanistically plausible despite low PLM plausibility (which actually supports disruption).
AlphaMissense gives the strongest LOF-proxy signal in the pool (z=0.852); conservation (app 0.61) supports a functional role of Asp291.
Glycine in a linker/regulatory region; introduction of Asp could disturb domain packing between catalytic and regulatory halves.
Glycine-to-aspartate introduces a bulky charged side chain at a likely structurally constrained position, plausibly abolishing fold or function. Needs evidence confirmation.
AlphaMissense scores it benign (0.247) and ESM-1v finds it relatively plausible (0.0095, highest of pool), both arguing against strong LOF; replaced by a candidate with better expected damage.

rejection.reason: AlphaMissense scores it benign (0.247) and ESM-1v finds it relatively plausible (0.0095, highest of pool), both arguing against strong LOF; replaced by a candidate with better expected damage.

history.rationale: With G441D rejected on benign phenotype evidence, add R157Q: Arg157 lies in the conserved FAD-binding catalytic N-terminal domain and charge-removing substitutions at such conserved basic residues are classic severe-MTHFR-deficiency mutations; needs phenotype/MSA confirmation next round.

Charge-removing substitution at a conserved basic residue in the catalytic FAD-binding domain; classic severe-MTHFR-deficiency mechanism, but still lacks direct phenotype evidence — needs phenotype/MSA call next round.
